verdicts.quote: a file is imported entirely or not at all.
a table of row errors (line, email, problem in words).
if `exists@example.com` appears on two lines, the first returns `already_exists` and the second `duplicate_in_file`.
whether any admin may create other admins (A-14 assumes yes, audited).
verdicts.missing: The spec assumes every admin can grant admin. It leaves open how to check the requested role against the individual importer’s grant authority.

verdicts.quote: available only to an authenticated user who is an administrator *at the time the request is authorised and again at commit*.
verdicts.missing: The relationship between permission to create a single user and permission to bulk-import users is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: line 1 is the header. … Required columns: `email`, `name`. Optional column: `role`. … stop row processing and create nothing: `missing_column` (one entry per missing required column, naming it), `unknown_column` (naming it)
quoted fields may contain commas and newlines, CRLF or LF record separators, an optional UTF-8 byte-order mark ignored
If any file-level or row error exists, no user is created … It sets no password, sends no email or invitation, and starts no session

size and row-count limits are configured values (`max_bytes`, `max_rows`, the latter counting data rows, header excluded); exceeding either rejects the whole file before any user is created (G-1: default values unresolved).
verdicts.missing: The production limits remain open. The acceptance cases supply values only for tests.

verdicts.quote: a 0-byte file returns `empty_file`; `email,name,role\n` returns `no_data_rows` … a one-data-row file creates one user.
Repeating a successful upload creates nothing and reports `already_exists` for every row
The request is parsed, validated and committed inside the single request, and the response is the final outcome.
verdicts.missing: The response tells the admin when synchronous processing finishes. Background processing for large files and completion reporting for such jobs are outside the specified flow.

verdicts.quote: It sets no password, sends no email or invitation, and starts no session
It sets no password, sends no email or invitation, and starts no session (A-12). How a created user first gains access is a separate capability (G-7).
verdicts.missing: The account’s initial active or pending status and the means of first sign-in remain open.

verdicts.quote: The file is parsed from the request stream/memory and is not written to the store, object storage or a cache. … any temporary file created by the platform's multipart handling is removed when the request ends, including on failure
`import_id`, actor id, time of completion, `outcome`, `rows_total`, `rows_created`, and a count per error code.
The file can be replaced and sent again.
verdicts.missing: The spec describes resubmitting a corrected file. It gives no cancellation behavior for an in-flight request or operation for retrying only its failed rows.

verdicts.quote: An import at the row limit must finish inside the hosting platform's request time limit … the page shows upload progress while bytes are sent, then an indeterminate "Creating users…" once sending is complete.
verdicts.missing: The platform deadline is unknown, leaving no concrete maximum duration. During server processing the admin sees a busy indicator without a measure of work completed.

verdicts.quote: The import only creates; it never updates, overwrites or merges an existing user.
verdicts.missing: The spec gives no requirement preserving the existing manual single-user creation workflow.

verdicts.quote: The import does not neutralise spreadsheet-formula prefixes (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) in stored values; that is the duty of any future export … `name`: non-empty after trimming (a maximum length is unresolved, G-3)
verdicts.missing: Formula handling for a spreadsheet export is deferred. The builder still needs a name-length limit and a row error for exceeding it.
